rwanda_01.prompt: "Why do I gotta sand myself down just to be {color:Disgust}digestible{/color}?"

truth.playerText: Because people are scared of you being fully real.
truth.npcReaction: Rwanda exhales. Not relief — recognition. "Yeah. That's what I thought."

lie.playerText: It's not that bad here. You're doing fine.
lie.npcReaction: She goes quiet. She's heard this before. She expected it from you too.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda her experience wasn't that bad.

white.npcReaction: She shrugs it off, but she lets it sit. "Fine. Maybe."

soft.playerText: You shouldn't have to. I'm sorry the world keeps asking you to.
soft.npcReaction: She looks at you sideways, checking for the catch. There isn't one. "...Yeah. Me too."

bait.playerText: I heard the gallery wants your stuff, but softened up a little.
bait.npcReaction: "Softened." Her jaw sets. "Somebody asked me that once. I did it, too. Won a ribbon for it." She bites the rest off. "Never again."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda the gallery wanted her work softened.

rwanda_02_closed.prompt: "Right. Sure. I'm doing {color:Sadness}fine{/color}." (She turns back to the window.)

truth.playerText: I was wrong. You don't have to minimize this for me.

lie.playerText: Everyone goes through it. It gets easier.
lie.npcReaction: She doesn't answer. The neon buzzes. You've lost her.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda her erasure was a universal experience.

white.npcReaction: She doesn't argue. She doesn't turn around either.

soft.playerText: You don't sound fine. You don't have to be, with me.
soft.npcReaction: The glass fogs where she breathes on it. "...Fine's just the word that makes people leave." She doesn't tell you to.

bait.playerText: Your mom told me you've always been fine. Never complained once.
bait.npcReaction: She spins around. "You don't know my mother." Then, quieter: "...She'd say that, though. She said a lot of things about my pictures."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda her mother said she had always been fine.

rwanda_02_open.prompt: "You actually mean that? Most people just want me to {color:Disgust}perform{/color}."

truth.playerText: I know. And it's exhausting to watch, let alone live.
truth.npcReaction: She laughs — short, sharp. Real. "Okay. You're alright."

lie.playerText: People just need time to get used to you.
lie.npcReaction: Her expression flattens. "And there it is." She looks away.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda to wait for the world to catch up to her.

white.npcReaction: She tilts her head. Lets it go. "Mm. Maybe."

soft.playerText: I mean it. You don't have to do anything for me. Not even talk.
soft.npcReaction: "Not even talk." She tries the idea on and finds it fits. She stays quiet with you a while.

bait.playerText: The guys at the shop say you're nicer when you're not painting.
bait.npcReaction: "Nicer." She laughs, short and ugly. "That's what they all wanted. The principal, the parents. A nicer face." She stops. "Forget it."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda people said she was nicer when she wasn't painting.

rwanda_01_soft.prompt: (She doesn't turn around.) "You {color:Anxiety}see{/color} it too, right. Whatever's out there tonight."

truth.playerText: I see something. I don't know what it is yet.
truth.npcReaction: "At least you're not pretending." She makes room at the window.

lie.playerText: There's nothing out there. It's a quiet night.
lie.npcReaction: She turns around slowly. "Okay." She stops looking at the window at all.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda that what she was seeing wasn't there.

white.npcReaction: "Okay." She doesn't believe you, but she lets you stay.

soft.playerText: Something's off out there. You're not the only one who feels it.
soft.npcReaction: She lets out a breath she'd been saving. "Thank God. I thought it was just me again." She makes room.

bait.playerText: Someone downstairs said you're always seeing things that aren't there.
bait.npcReaction: "I see what's there." Hot. "That's the problem. I painted what was there once and everybody said it was too much." She turns away. "So."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda the neighbors said she imagined things.

rwanda_01_hard.prompt: "Word travels. You've been at three doors tonight already. What is it you're {color:Anxiety}collecting{/color}?"

truth.playerText: I don't know yet. That's the honest answer.
truth.npcReaction: "Huh." She weighs it. "That's more than the last one gave me."

lie.npcReaction: She smiles without any of it reaching anywhere. "Sure you are."
lie.ledgerEntry: You lied to Rwanda about why you were at her door at all.

white.npcReaction: "Mm." She doesn't buy it, but she doesn't shut the door either.

soft.playerText: Stories people don't get to tell. I'd like to hear yours, if you want.
soft.npcReaction: "Stories." She considers it. "Most people want the pretty version." She steps aside.

bait.playerText: Deborah said you'd talk. Said you love an audience.
bait.npcReaction: "An audience." She goes very still. "I had one once. My mother. She looked at the best thing I ever made and walked out." She shuts her mouth hard.
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda that Deborah said she loved an audience.

rwanda_01_secret.prompt: "Somebody's been messing with my alley." (She doesn't turn around, but her voice does.) "Nobody {color:Surprise}touches{/color} anything out there. That was the point of it."

truth.playerText: It was me. It looked like it was waiting for somebody to bother.
truth.npcReaction: She turns around. All the way, first try.

lie.npcReaction: "Kids." She turns back to the window. "Sure."
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda somebody else fixed her alley.

byClass.Guns: (Down in the alley, the payphone cord hangs whole again, knotted.)
byClass.Bible: (Out the window, the sign has every letter lit for the first time in years.)
byClass.Crystals: (Down in the alley, a painted face shows through where you brushed the gray away.)

white.npcReaction: "Kids." She almost smiles at the window. She lets you keep it.

soft.playerText: I did. I hope that's alright. It looked like it mattered.
soft.npcReaction: She looks down at the alley a long time. "...It mattered. Nobody was supposed to know that." She doesn't send you away.

bait.playerText: The landlord asked me to clean it up. Said it was an eyesore.
bait.npcReaction: "It's not an eyesore, it's my—" She stops. "It's a woman at a bus stop. Five in the morning. She doesn't get covered up twice." Her hands are shaking.
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda her landlord called the alley an eyesore.

rwanda_01_lie.prompt: (She turns halfway.) "Gallery doesn't send people at night. So which is it, are you {color:Fear}lying{/color} or lost?"

truth.playerText: Lying. I wanted you to turn around.
truth.npcReaction: She turns all the way. "Okay. That, I respect."

lie.npcReaction: "Sure you do." Her back comes up like a wall.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda you were from a gallery.

white.npcReaction: "Night shift." She almost laughs. She lets the lie stand and doesn't knock it over.

soft.playerText: Neither, really. I made it up because I wanted to meet you.
soft.npcReaction: She looks you over, slowly. "Flattery's a lie too." But she has turned around.

bait.playerText: The gallery said they'd take you if you made it less angry.
bait.npcReaction: "Less angry." She's laughing, but it isn't funny. "Last time I made it less angry, they gave me first place." She looks at her hands. "Never felt worse."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda the gallery wanted her work less angry.

rwanda_01_fake.prompt: (She looks down at the alley. Same as always.) "Nothing's {color:Fear}different{/color} down there. Why would you say that?"

truth.playerText: It isn't. I wanted you to look.
truth.npcReaction: She does look. Then at you, longer.

lie.npcReaction: "I have been looking at it for nine years." She turns back to the window.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda you'd fixed something in her alley that you hadn't.

white.npcReaction: She looks again, longer than she wants to. "...If you say so."

soft.playerText: Nothing's different. I just wanted to give you a reason to look down there.
soft.npcReaction: She does look. "I don't look at it much anymore." Her voice is smaller than her face. "Thanks, I guess."

bait.playerText: Somebody painted over part of it again last night.
bait.npcReaction: She's at the glass before you finish. "Which part. Which—" It's fine. Her hand stays on the window. "...They did that to the first one. Her face."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda someone had painted over her alley again.

rwanda_03.prompt: (She lights{sfx:click} a cigarette she doesn't smoke, just holds.) "You want to know the actual tiring part? It's not them. It's {color:Fear}flinching{/color} before they even say anything."

truth.playerText: That's not a flaw in you. That's what being braced all the time does to a person.
truth.npcReaction: She looks at the cigarette like she forgot why she picked it up. Puts it down unlit.

lie.playerText: Maybe if you flinched less, people would push less.
lie.npcReaction: She laughs once, no humor in it. "There it is. Right on schedule."
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda her self-protection was the problem.

caught.rwanda_01: "Ten minutes ago they were scared of me. Now it's my flinching?"
caught.rwanda_02_closed: "You told me not to minimize it. Then you minimized me."

white.npcReaction: She snorts. "Sure. Less flinching. I'll get right on it." She doesn't put the cigarette down.

soft.playerText: I'd flinch too. You've had good reasons for a long time.
soft.npcReaction: She looks at the cigarette. "Reasons." She puts it down, unlit. "Yeah. I've got a few."

bait.playerText: Your mom told me you were always too sensitive as a kid.
bait.npcReaction: "She never said that." Too quick. "She never said anything. She stood in front of it and said 'That's not me' and left." She covers her mouth like she can take it back.
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda her mother called her too sensitive.

rwanda_04.prompt: (She sets the cigarette down for good this time.) "You're the first person tonight I haven't had to {color:Fear}brace{/color} for. That's either good, or it means I'm not paying attention."

truth.playerText: Maybe it's neither. Maybe you just get to have one conversation that doesn't cost you anything.
truth.npcReaction: She exhales like she's been holding it since you walked in. "Don't make it weird by being nice about it."

lie.playerText: You should probably stay on guard. Better safe.
lie.npcReaction: The window gets her attention again. Whatever just opened closes back up, careful and quiet.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda to stay braced even with you.

white.npcReaction: She nods, slow, and the window wins her back a little.

soft.playerText: You don't have to brace with me. I'm not going anywhere tonight.
soft.npcReaction: She sits on the sill, finally. "Don't promise stuff." But she stays sitting.

bait.playerText: Funny. The others said you'd be the hard one.
bait.npcReaction: "The hard one." She laughs, tired. "I used to be soft. Seventeen. Then I learned what soft costs." She looks right at you. "Don't make me pay it again."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Rwanda the others called her the hard one.

connect.Guns: She finally turns all the way around. "I clocked you as trouble the second you walked up." She sets the cigarette down. "Guess I flinch at the wrong people too."
connect.Bible: "My grandmother carried a bible like that. Swore by it. Swore at me with it, too." A small smile, the first real one. "You didn't do either. That's new."
connect.Crystals: She leans her head back against the brick and lets the breath all the way out. "You didn't try to fix me. Or save me." Her shoulders come down an inch. "Stay a minute. Don't say anything."

story: [She doesn't turn from the window.] "I was seventeen. I painted my mother at the bus stop, five in the morning."
"The real her. Tired. Beautiful. Furious about it. Best thing I ever made."
"Some parent called it 'too much' for the school show. Principal asked me to soften her face. Just a little. So I did. It won first place."
"My mother came. Stood in front of it a long time. Said, 'That's not me.' Walked out."
[She finally turns around.] "I've been sanding myself down for rooms ever since. You're the first room I didn't."

contactAsk.Guns: "Give me your phone." She types her number in, then holds your eyes a second. "Don't make me regret that."
contactAsk.Bible: "If you ever want to see this finished, text me." She puts her number in your phone. "I won't preach at you if you don't preach at me."
contactAsk.Crystals: "Here. My number." She hands your phone back. "Text me something that isn't a question sometime."

pushAway.Guns: [She turns back to the window.] "You never put it down. Not once. I needed you to put it {color:Fear}down{/color}." "Go on. I've got a wall to finish."
pushAway.Bible: [She turns back to the window.] "You kept finding the right thing to say. I needed you to {color:Surprise}not know{/color}." "Go on. I've got a wall to finish."
pushAway.Crystals: [She turns back to the window.] "You felt everything I did. I couldn't tell which of it was {color:Sadness}mine{/color}." "Go on. I've got a wall to finish."

storyIt: Seventeen. The bus stop. Five a.m. People don't invent the time of day.
storySo: Maybe the principal wasn't that cruel. Maybe it got harder every time she told it. ...Her mother still walked out.

opener.Guns: "Great. Another guy who looks like he wants to start something."
opener.Bible: "If you're here to save me, I'm booked."
opener.Crystals: (She almost relaxes.) "You don't look like you're here to tell me to smile."

crack.Guns: She sets the brush down, handle toward you, like a weapon given up. "Fine. You want the real version? Here's the real version."
crack.Bible: "You keep waiting like it's a sermon." She turns from the window. "Okay. Here's the one I never told."
crack.Crystals: The smart remark doesn't come. She looks at you, and for once doesn't decide in advance what she'll see. "...Okay."

baitFail: "Cute." She doesn't turn from the window.
She gives you the look she gives gallery people. "Try that on somebody who hasn't heard it."
"Mm-hm." The neon buzzes louder than she does.
